rationale: The shed camera (cam_shed) showed RSSI -87 dBm, below the -80 dBm threshold documented in the manual as causing intermittent disconnections and choppy live view. Logs confirmed 9 heartbeat losses in 24h with reconnects at -87 dBm, while all other devices and the base station were normal. Installing the RP-1 repeater resolved the issue (camera stable for two days), confirming a weak-signal root cause rather than a hardware fault.

repair_steps: Confirm the RP-1 repeater is installed between the base station and the shed camera.
Verify the shed camera RSSI is now above -80 dBm (preferably above -70 dBm) in Device Settings > Device Info.
Check that the shed camera has remained online with no heartbeat losses for at least 48 hours.
If stable, close the case as resolved.
output.customer_reply: We're glad the repeater resolved the issue. Your shed camera now has a stable connection. If you experience any further problems, please don't hesitate to reach out. Thank you for your patience!

results.text: Peripherals talk to the base station over a sub-GHz proprietary radio. Signal strength (RSSI) is shown in Device Settings > Device Info. Above -70 dBm is good, -70 to -80 dBm is acceptable, below -80 dBm causes intermittent disconnections, delayed notifications and choppy live view. Concrete walls, metal doors and fridges strongly attenuate the signal. Fix: move the device or base station, or install the official RP-1 repeater.
Customer reported a CAM-S1 in a detached garage going offline several times a day. RSSI was -86 dBm; all other devices normal. Installing an RP-1 repeater solved it. Resolved at frontline.
